sanskrit: tatas tad amṛtāsvādaṃ gṛdhrarājena bhāṣitam niśamya vadato hṛṣṭās te vacaḥ plavagarṣabhāḥ
english: Then, having heard those words of the king of vultures — words sweet as nectar — those foremost of monkeys were filled with joy as he spoke.

sanskrit: jāmbavān vai hariśreṣṭhaḥ saha sarvaiḥ plavaṃgamaiḥ bhūtalāt sahasotthāya gṛdhrarājānam abravīt
english: Jāmbavān, the foremost of monkeys, together with all the leaping ones, suddenly rose from the ground and addressed the king of vultures.

sanskrit: kva sītā kena vā dṛṣṭā ko vā harati maithilīm tad ākhyātu bhavān sarvaṃ gatir bhava vanaukasām
english: "Where is Sītā? By whom was she seen? Or who has carried off the daughter of Mithilā? Tell us all of this, sir — be a guide to us forest-dwellers."

sanskrit: ko dāśarathibāṇānāṃ vajraveganipātinām svayaṃ lakṣmaṇam uktānāṃ na cintayati vikramam
english: "Who would not regard the valor of the arrows of Daśaratha's son — falling with the speed of the thunderbolt — and of Lakṣmaṇa himself, who has been spoken of?"

sanskrit: sa harīn prītisaṃyuktān sītā śrutisamāhitān punar āśvāsayan prīta idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: He, pleased, reassuring those monkeys who were filled with affection and attentive to hear of Sītā, spoke these words again.

sanskrit: śrūyatām iha vaidehyā yathā me haraṇaṃ śrutam yena cāpi mamākhyātaṃ yatra cāyatalocanā
english: "Hear now how the abduction of the Vaidehi was heard by me, by whom it was reported to me, and where the wide-eyed one is."

sanskrit: aham asmin girau durge bahuyojanam āyate cirān nipatito vṛddhaḥ kṣīṇaprāṇaparākramaḥ
english: "I, old and my vital strength and prowess diminished, fell long ago upon this difficult mountain extending many yojanas."

sanskrit: taṃ mām evaṃgataṃ putraḥ supārśvo nāma nāmataḥ āhāreṇa yathākālaṃ bibharti patatāṃ varaḥ
english: "My son, named Supārśva, foremost among birds, sustains me in this condition with food at the proper time."

sanskrit: tīkṣṇakāmās tu gandharvās tīkṣṇakopā bhujaṃgamāḥ mṛgāṇāṃ tu bhayaṃ tīkṣṇaṃ tatas tīkṣṇakṣudhā vayam
english: "Gandharvas are sharp in their desires, serpents sharp in their anger, beasts sharp in their fears — and we birds are sharp in our hunger."

sanskrit: sa kadā cit kṣudhārtasya mama cāhārakāṅkṣiṇaḥ gatasūryo 'hani prāpto mama putro hy anāmiṣaḥ
english: "Once, when the sun had set and I was afflicted by hunger and longing for food, my son came bringing no flesh."

sanskrit: sa mayā vṛddhabhāvāc ca kopāc ca paribhartsitaḥ kṣutpipāsā parītena kumāraḥ patatāṃ varaḥ
english: "That youth, foremost among birds, was rebuked by me — overcome by hunger and thirst, and on account of old age and anger."

sanskrit: sa mamāhārasaṃrodhāt pīḍitaḥ prītivardhanaḥ anumānya yathātattvam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: "He, the joy-increaser, distressed by my withholding of food, paid his respects and then spoke these words truthfully."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tāta yathākālam āmiṣārthī kham āplutaḥ mahendrasya girer dvāram āvṛtya ca samāsthitaḥ
english: "'Father, at the proper time I took to the sky in search of flesh, and stationed myself blocking the gateway of Mount Mahendra."

sanskrit: tatra sattvasahasrāṇāṃ sāgarāntaracāriṇām panthānam eko 'dhyavasaṃ saṃniroddhum avāṅmukhaḥ
english: "'There, facing downward, I alone set myself to obstruct the path of the thousands of creatures that roam the far reaches of the ocean."

sanskrit: tatra kaś cin mayā dṛṣṭaḥ sūryodayasamaprabhām striyam ādāya gacchan vai bhinnāñjanacayopamaḥ
english: "'There I saw someone resembling a heap of broken collyrium, carrying a woman blazing like the rising sun, and going away."

sanskrit: so 'ham abhyavahārārthī tau dṛṣṭvā kṛtaniścayaḥ tena sāmnā vinītena panthānam abhiyācitaḥ
english: "'I, bent on seizing food, had made my resolve upon seeing them, but I was entreated concerning the path by him with gentle conciliation."

sanskrit: na hi sāmopapannānāṃ prahartā vidyate kva cit nīceṣv api janaḥ kaś cit kim aṅga bata madvidhaḥ
english: "'Indeed, nowhere is there anyone who would strike those who approach with conciliation — not even some person of low birth, much less one like me."

sanskrit: sa yātas tejasā vyoma saṃkṣipann iva vegataḥ athāhaṃ khe carair bhūtair abhigamya sabhājitaḥ
english: "'He went through the sky with his brilliance, compressing it as it were with his speed. Then I was approached and honored by the aerial beings."

sanskrit: diṣṭyā jīvasi tāteti abruvan māṃ maharṣayaḥ kathaṃ cit sakalatro 'sau gatas te svasty asaṃśayam
english: "'"By good fortune you live, father," said the great seers to me. "He who passed with his wife has gone well — there is no doubt."""

sanskrit: evam uktas tato 'haṃ taiḥ siddhaiḥ paramaśobhanaiḥ sa ca me rāvaṇo rājā rakṣasāṃ prativeditaḥ
english: "'Thus addressed by those supremely splendid perfected sages, I was informed that he was Rāvaṇa, king of the rākṣasas."

sanskrit: haran dāśarather bhāryāṃ rāmasya janakātmajām bhraṣṭābharaṇakauśeyāṃ śokavegaparājitām
english: "'He was carrying off the wife of Daśaratha's son Rāma — Janaka's daughter — her ornaments fallen, clad in silk, overcome by the force of grief."

sanskrit: rāmalakṣmaṇayor nāma krośantīṃ muktamūrdhajām eṣa kālātyayas tāvad iti vākyavidāṃ varaḥ
english: "'She was crying out the names of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, her hair loosened. "This is a waste of time" — so said Supārśva, the foremost among those skilled in speech.'

sanskrit: etam arthaṃ samagraṃ me supārśvaḥ pratyavedayat tac chrutvāpi hi me buddhir nāsīt kā cit parākrame
english: "Supārśva reported all this matter in full to me. Yet even upon hearing this, my mind had no inclination toward any heroic action."

sanskrit: apakṣo hi kathaṃ pakṣī karma kiṃ cid upakramet yat tu śakyaṃ mayā kartuṃ vāgbuddhiguṇavartinā
english: "For how can a bird without wings undertake any deed? Yet what can be done by me — proceeding by the power of speech and intelligence —"

sanskrit: śrūyatāṃ tat pravakṣyāmi bhavatāṃ pauruṣāśrayam vāṅmatibhyāṃ hi sārveṣāṃ kariṣyāmi priyaṃ hi vaḥ yad dhi dāśaratheḥ kāryaṃ mama tan nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "Hear what I shall declare, relying on your valor. Through speech and thought I shall accomplish what is dear to all of you, for whatever is the task of Daśaratha's son is indeed mine — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: te bhavanto matiśreṣṭhā balavanto manasvinaḥ sahitāḥ kapirājena devair api durāsadāḥ
english: "You are supreme in wisdom, powerful, high-minded, united with the king of monkeys — unapproachable even by the gods."

sanskrit: rāmalakṣmaṇabāṇāś ca niśitāḥ kaṅkapatriṇaḥ trayāṇām api lokānāṃ paryāptās trāṇanigrahe
english: "And the sharpened arrows of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa, feathered with heron-plumes, suffice for protecting and subduing all three worlds."

sanskrit: kāmaṃ khalu daśagrīvas tejobalasamanvitaḥ bhavatāṃ tu samarthānāṃ na kiṃ cid api duṣkaram
english: "Indeed Daśagrīva is endowed with brilliance and strength — yet for you who are capable, nothing whatsoever is difficult."

sanskrit: tad alaṃ kālasaṃgena kriyatāṃ buddhiniścayaḥ na hi karmasu sajjante buddhimanto bhavadvidhāḥ
english: "Therefore, enough with the delay of time — let a firm resolve of the mind be made. For the wise, such as yourselves, do not hesitate in undertakings."

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛtodakaṃ snātaṃ taṃ gṛdhraṃ hariyūthapāḥ upaviṣṭā girau durge parivārya samantataḥ
english: Then the leaders of the monkey troops seated themselves on the difficult mountain all around that vulture who had bathed and performed his water-rites.

sanskrit: tam aṅgadam upāsīnaṃ taiḥ sarvair haribhir vṛtam janitapratyayo harṣāt saṃpātiḥ punar abravīt
english: Saṃpāti, his trust established, spoke again with joy to Aṅgada seated there, surrounded by all those monkeys.

sanskrit: kṛtvā niḥśabdam ekāgrāḥ śṛṇvantu harayo mama tattvaṃ saṃkīrtayiṣyāmi yathā jānāmi maithilīm
english: "Let the monkeys fall silent and listen with one-pointed attention. I shall declare truthfully, as I know it, where the daughter of Mithilā is."

sanskrit: asya vindhyasya śikhare patito 'smi purā vane sūryātapaparītāṅgo nirdagdhaḥ sūryaraśmibhiḥ
english: "I fell long ago upon the summit of this Vindhya in the forest, my limbs overcome by the heat of the sun, burnt by the rays of the sun."

sanskrit: labdhasaṃjñas tu ṣaḍrātrād vivaśo vihvalann iva vīkṣamāṇo diśaḥ sarvā nābhijānāmi kiṃ cana
english: "Regaining consciousness only after six nights, helpless and bewildered as it were, scanning all directions, I knew nothing at all."

sanskrit: tatas tu sāgarāñ śailān nadīḥ sarvāḥ sarāṃsi ca vanāny aṭavideśāṃś ca samīkṣya matir āgamat
english: "Then, surveying the oceans, mountains, all rivers and lakes, forests and wilderness regions, my understanding returned."

sanskrit: hṛṣṭapakṣigaṇākīrṇaḥ kandarāntarakūṭavān dakṣiṇasyodadhes tīre vindhyo 'yam iti niścitaḥ
english: "Filled with flocks of joyful birds, having peaks and cave-interiors, on the shore of the southern ocean — I concluded: 'This is the Vindhya.'"

sanskrit: āsīc cātrāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ surair api supūjitam ṛṣir niśākaro nāma yasminn ugratapābhavat
english: "And here there was a holy hermitage, honored even by the gods, in which the sage named Niśākara practiced severe austerities."

sanskrit: aṣṭau varṣasahasrāṇi tenāsminn ṛṣiṇā vinā vasato mama dharmajñāḥ svargate tu niśākare
english: "Eight thousand years I dwelt here, O knowers of dharma, without that sage — for Niśākara had gone to heaven."

sanskrit: avatīrya ca vindhyāgrāt kṛcchreṇa viṣamāc chanaiḥ tīkṣṇadarbhāṃ vasumatīṃ duḥkhena punar āgataḥ
english: "Descending with difficulty and slowly from the uneven summit of the Vindhya, I returned with hardship to the earth sharp with kuśa-grass."

sanskrit: tam ṛṣiṃ draṣṭu kāmo 'smi duḥkhenābhyāgato bhṛśam jaṭāyuṣā mayā caiva bahuśo 'bhigato hi saḥ
english: "Desirous of seeing that sage, I came with great difficulty; for that sage had been visited many times by Jaṭāyu and by me."

sanskrit: tasyāśramapadābhyāśe vavur vātāḥ sugandhinaḥ vṛkṣo nāpuṣpitaḥ kaś cid aphalo vā na dṛśyate
english: "Near the site of his hermitage, sweet-scented winds blew; no tree was seen that was not flowering or not bearing fruit."

sanskrit: upetya cāśramaṃ puṇyaṃ vṛkṣamūlam upāśritaḥ draṣṭukāmaḥ pratīkṣe ca bhagavantaṃ niśākaram
english: "And having arrived at the holy hermitage and taken shelter at the foot of a tree, desiring to see him, I waited for the blessed Niśākara."

sanskrit: athāpaśyam adūrastham ṛṣiṃ jvalitatejasaṃ kṛtābhiṣekaṃ durdharṣam upāvṛttam udaṅmukham
english: "Then I saw the sage not far off — blazing with energy, having completed his ablutions, irresistible, turned face northward."

sanskrit: tam ṛkṣāḥ sṛmarā vyāghrāḥ siṃhā nāgāḥ sarīsṛpāḥ parivāryopagacchanti dātāraṃ prāṇino yathā
english: "Bears, deer, tigers, lions, elephants, and serpents came surrounding him, as living beings approach a benefactor."

sanskrit: tataḥ prāptam ṛṣiṃ jñātvā tāni sattvāni vai yayuḥ praviṣṭe rājani yathā sarvaṃ sāmātyakaṃ balam
english: "Then, knowing the sage had arrived, those creatures departed, as all the ministers and forces withdraw when the king has entered."

sanskrit: ṛṣis tu dṛṣṭvā māṃ tuṣṭaḥ praviṣṭaś cāśramaṃ punaḥ muhūrtamātrān niṣkramya tataḥ kāryam apṛcchata
english: "But the sage, seeing me, was pleased, entered the hermitage again, and after just a moment came out and asked about my purpose."

sanskrit: saumya vaikalyatāṃ dṛṣṭvā roṃṇāṃ te nāvagamyate agnidagdhāv imau pakṣau tvak caiva vraṇitā tava
english: "'Gentle one, seeing the loss of your feathers I do not comprehend — these two wings of yours are burnt by fire, and your skin too is wounded."

sanskrit: dvau gṛdhrau dṛṣṭapūrvau me mātariśvasamau jave gṛdhrāṇāṃ caiva rājānau bhrātarau kāmarūpiṇau
english: "'Two vultures have been seen by me before, equal to the wind in speed, kings of vultures, brothers who could assume any form at will."

sanskrit: jyeṣṭhas tvaṃ tu ca saṃpātir jaṭāyur anujas tava mānuṣaṃ rūpam āsthāya gṛhṇītāṃ caraṇau mama
english: "'You are Saṃpāti the elder, and Jaṭāyu is your younger brother. Assuming a human form, let them both grasp my feet."

sanskrit: kiṃ te vyādhisamutthānaṃ pakṣayoḥ patanaṃ katham daṇḍo vāyaṃ dhṛtaḥ kena sarvam ākhyāhi pṛcchataḥ
english: "'What is the origin of your affliction? How did the fall of your wings come about? Or has this punishment been imposed by someone? Tell me all, as I ask.'"

sanskrit: tatas tad dāruṇaṃ karma duṣkaraṃ sāhasāt kṛtam ācacakṣe muneḥ sarvaṃ sūryānugamanaṃ tathā
english: Then Saṃpāti narrated to the sage in full that terrible deed done rashly and with difficulty — and likewise the pursuit of the sun.

sanskrit: bhagavan vraṇayuktatvāl lajjayā cākulendriyaḥ pariśrānto na śaknomi vacanaṃ paribhāṣitum
english: "Blessed one, on account of my wounds and with senses disturbed by shame, I am exhausted and cannot speak at length."

sanskrit: ahaṃ caiva jaṭāyuś ca saṃgharṣād darpamohitau ākāśaṃ patitau vīrau jighāsantau parākramam
english: "Both I and Jaṭāyu, deluded by pride through rivalry, being heroes, soared into the sky wishing to surpass each other's valor."

sanskrit: kailāsaśikhare baddhvā munīnām agrataḥ paṇam raviḥ syād anuyātavyo yāvad astaṃ mahāgirim
english: "Having made a wager on the summit of Kailāsa before the sages, the sun was to be followed until it reached the great western mountain of setting."

sanskrit: athāvāṃ yugapat prāptāv apaśyāva mahītale rathacakrapramāṇāni nagarāṇi pṛthak pṛthak
english: "Then we two, arriving simultaneously, looked down at the earth's surface and saw separate cities the size of chariot wheels."

sanskrit: kva cid vāditraghoṣāṃś ca brahmaghoṣāṃś ca śuśruva gāyantīś cāṅganā bahvīḥ paśyāvo raktavāsasaḥ
english: "Somewhere we heard the sounds of musical instruments and the sounds of Vedic recitation, and we saw many women singing, clothed in red garments."

sanskrit: tūrṇam utpatya cākāśam ādityapatham āsthitau āvām ālokayāvas tad vanaṃ śādvalasaṃsthitam
english: "Swiftly soaring and taking the path of the sun, we two looked back and saw that forest carpeted in green grass."

sanskrit: upalair iva saṃchannā dṛśyate bhūḥ śiloccayaiḥ āpagābhiś ca saṃvītā sūtrair iva vasuṃdharā
english: "The earth appeared covered as if by smooth stones — by masses of rock, and the earth was wrapped with rivers as if by threads."

sanskrit: himavāṃś caiva vindhyaś ca meruś ca sumahān nagaḥ bhūtale saṃprakāśante nāgā iva jalāśaye
english: "The Himavat and the Vindhya and the very great mountain Meru appeared on the earth's surface like serpents in a lake."

sanskrit: tīvrasvedaś ca khedaś ca bhayaṃ cāsīt tadāvayoḥ samāviśata mohaś ca mohān mūrchā ca dāruṇā
english: "Intense perspiration and distress and fear beset us both then; confusion overcame us, and from confusion a terrible swooning."

sanskrit: na dig vijñāyate yāmyā nāgenyā na ca vāruṇī yugānte niyato loko hato dagdha ivāgninā
english: "The southern direction could not be distinguished, nor the northeastern, nor the western — the world was fixed as at the end of an age, stricken, as if consumed by fire."

sanskrit: yatnena mahatā bhūyo raviḥ samavalokitaḥ tulyaḥ pṛthvīpramāṇena bhāskaraḥ pratibhāti nau
english: "With great effort the sun was perceived once more — the maker of light appeared to us as equal in extent to the entire earth."

sanskrit: jaṭāyur mām anāpṛcchya nipapāta mahīṃ tataḥ taṃ dṛṣṭvā tūrṇam ākāśād ātmānaṃ muktavān aham
english: "Jaṭāyu, without asking me, plunged down to the earth. Seeing him, I swiftly released myself from the sky."

sanskrit: pakṣibhyāṃ ca mayā gupto jaṭāyur na pradahyata pramādāt tatra nirdagdhaḥ patan vāyupathād aham
english: "Shielded by my wings, Jaṭāyu was not burnt; but through my own negligence I was completely burnt there, falling from the wind-path."

sanskrit: āśaṅke taṃ nipatitaṃ janasthāne jaṭāyuṣam ahaṃ tu patito vindhye dagdhapakṣo jaḍīkṛtaḥ
english: "I suspect that Jaṭāyu fell in Janasthāna; but I fell on the Vindhya, with burnt wings, rendered motionless."

sanskrit: rājyena hīno bhrātrā ca pakṣābhyāṃ vikrameṇa ca sarvathā martum evecchan patiṣye śikharād gireḥ
english: "Bereft of my kingdom, of my brother, of both wings and of my valor, wishing in every way only to die, I shall fall from the mountain peak."
